title: MCP Tools and Resources
content: An MCP tool performs a focused action that a client can call, while an MCP resource exposes data that a client can read. Tools should use clear action-based names and validate their inputs.

title: MCP Inspector Basics
content: The MCP Inspector can discover registered tools, display their input schemas, send test arguments, and show the responses returned by the MCP server.

title: Zod Schema Validation
content: Zod schemas validate tool inputs before the tool handler runs. Required strings can be trimmed and checked for minimum and maximum length, while numeric limits can be restricted to positive integers.

title: Git Branch Workflow
content: New project tasks should be completed on feature branches instead of directly on main. Each branch should contain focused commits and be reviewed through a Pull Request before it is merged.

title: Offline Fixture Data
content: Fixture data is sample data committed inside the repository. Local fixtures make demos reliable because the project can continue working without internet access or external API services.
